propositions: When a compaction sweep holds the store write lock, blocked sessions see only a bare PID in LockTimeout errors, making it impossible to determine if interrupting the holder is safe.
The lock acquisition path must stamp the holder with an operation label (`op=compact-sweep`) so that `describe_lock_holder` can render it into error messages and identify interruptible operations.
An ambient `contextvars.ContextVar` carries the operation label from sweep entry points through to `_owner_stamp` without modifying individual acquisition call sites like `_compact_locked`.
The v2 lock stamp format must remain colon-free and forward-compatible; the `op=` field is sanitized and ignored by staleness reclamation logic.

LockTimeout messages must include a remedy statement when the holder is recognized as a known interruptible operation (like `compact-sweep`), indicating data loss is impossible and the next trigger will re-fold.
